summary: Backend-only testing of new Web Push (Service Worker) endpoints in /app/backend/server.py. Created /app/backend/tests/test_push.py covering VAPID public key, admin auth gating, subscribe upsert/idempotency, Pydantic validation (422 on missing keys), unsubscribe, send-test resilience against malformed keys, and marketing regression. All 15 push tests pass; all 18 prior marketing tests still pass. Backend logs confirm '[push] daily-reminder scheduler started' on startup. send-test never returned 500 even with fake keys/endpoint and gracefully returned {sent, failed, subscriptions}.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 3659 lines — should be split into routers/services modules (admin, marketing, push, jobs, etc.) for maintainability.

Push subscribe/unsubscribe rely entirely on the global admin_auth_middleware; consider also adding an explicit Depends(get_admin_user) on each route as defense-in-depth in case the middleware is ever bypassed/refactored.

send-test endpoint loops _send_webpush synchronously inside an async route — for many subscriptions this will block the event loop. Consider asyncio.to_thread or run_in_executor (works fine today since one admin browser = ~1 subscription, but worth noting).

_send_daily_reminder uses 'singleton' as marketing_settings _id; a stricter Pydantic validator on reminder_hour at write time (already present 0-23) is good — but we could also persist last_sent_date inside the same doc atomically to avoid double-sending across restarts.
PushSubscriptionKeys.dict() is deprecated in Pydantic v2; prefer .model_dump(). Not a bug — just future-proofing.
seed_data_creation: Tests create transient push_subscriptions docs with TEST_-prefixed FCM endpoints and clean them up via /api/admin/push/unsubscribe in the same test or finally block. No persistent test data left behind.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Web Push backend is fully covered by /app/backend/tests/test_push.py (15 tests). Marketing regression is /app/backend/tests/test_marketing.py (18 tests). Scheduler runs every 60s — do NOT add timing-based assertions; rely on log line '[push] daily-reminder scheduler started'. Use _fake_subscription() helper for any future tests that need a parseable-but-undeliverable PushSubscription. send-test must always return 200 even with bad keys.
rca of the issue: N/A — no issues found. All review-request acceptance criteria pass: VAPID key returns 200 publicly; subscribe/unsubscribe/send-test require admin cookie (401 without); subscribe is idempotent (delete returns deleted=1 after two subscribes of same endpoint); validation returns 422 on missing keys.p256dh / keys.auth / endpoint; send-test returns graceful JSON with failed>=1 against fake endpoint, never 500; scheduler boots cleanly per backend logs; existing marketing endpoints unaffected.
